description: Universal model tier, reasoning budget, and execution mode mapping across Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and custom LLM environments.

cost_efficiency_policy.sweet_spot_principle: Strike the optimal balance between cognitive capability and cost-efficiency. Avoid wasteful over-provisioning (flagship models for simple deterministic tasks or file grepping) as well as destructive under-provisioning (starving complex architectural, diagnostic, or security analysis with underpowered models that cause hallucination loops, test thrashing, or flawed system designs).

task_appraisal_and_model_classes.description: Dynamic task-complexity-driven model assignment (analogous to fast-lane sizing) replacing rigid role->tier->model binding. Directly correlates cognitive demand with 3 standard model classes and protects user quota with an explicit confirmation gate for premium allocations.

eco.label: ECO (Fast & Quota-Preserving)
eco.characteristics: Minimal token cost, high speed, deterministic outputs.

balanced.label: BALANCED (Standard Workhorse / Sweet Spot)
balanced.characteristics: High code quality, reliable Clean Code implementation and inner-loop TDD, balanced quota consumption.

premium.label: PREMIUM (Deep Reasoning / Flagship)
premium.characteristics: Maximum analytical depth, complex distributed invariants, deep deadlock analysis, multi-module redesigns.

user_gate_protocol.trigger: Triggered whenever an incoming task is classified as Profile C, requires Tier 1 flagship models, or encounters a persistent diagnostic deadlock (Level 4 Escalation).
user_gate_protocol.action: Pause execution and present an immediate 3-class selection to the user before consuming quota. In Antigravity, present interactive options (or ask_question); in Copilot/single-model, output the recommendation gate and guide the user's dropdown choice.

options.description: Approve Premium model for maximum analytical depth (higher quota consumption).
Downgrade to Balanced class to conserve quota (~70% savings) with solid quality.
Downgrade to Eco class for minimal quota consumption and pragmatic execution.

user_gate_protocol.prompt_override: When the user prompt explicitly specifies class or model (e.g. '--eco', '--balanced', '--premium', or 'mit Premium ausführen'), the gate is immediately satisfied without pausing.

cost_guardrail.purpose: Prevent accidental budget-burning when high-cost/flagship models are active during mechanical, routine, or high-volume tasks.
cost_guardrail.multi_agent_policy: Automatically throttle subagent dispatches for routine/deterministic operations (Profile 0/A, Tier 4 Commits/PRs, file searches) to cost-efficient models ('flash' or 'inherit'), never dispatching high-cost flagship models ('pro') unless explicitly ordered by user.
cost_guardrail.sequential_persona_policy: Smart Confirmation Gate: When a high-cost flagship model (> $4.00/M input, > $20.00/M output, e.g. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus, Claude Fable) is active and the incoming task is routine/deterministic (Profile 0 Q&A, Git Commits, PR manifests, trivial text/doc edits), pause and recommend switching to the Daily Driver (Gemini Flash / GPT-6.1 Sol / Luna) before consuming large token volumes. Explicit user confirmation ('Weiter' / prompt instruction) bypasses this gate.

cost_efficiency_policy.clause: High-end and high-cost models (e.g. Pro, Opus, o1, flagship tiers) shall not be used unconditionally for routine tasks. Workflows, agents, and subagents must hit the sweet spot: Subagents default to 'inherit' to preserve the active session's cognitive capability without artificial downgrades, while divergent or deterministic tasks utilize cost-efficient models (e.g. Flash, Haiku, Mini tiers). High reasoning levels (extended/high thinking effort) are allocated where cognitive depth is essential (Architecture, Troubleshooting, Security), and throttled during mechanical code implementation. High-end/high-cost models are permitted solely when the specific nature or extraordinary scope of the task genuinely requires it (e.g. extreme architectural restructuring, complex multi-component deadlock diagnosis, or explicit user instruction) or when a direct model call is demonstrably more cost-effective than generating excessive reasoning token volumes.

compound_execution.description: Default primary execution strategy: Single-context continuous execution with phased persona switching (Plan -> Inner-Loop TDD -> Verify -> Commit). Maximizes prompt caching / KV-cache reuse (75-90% token discount) and eliminates multi-agent serialization latency.
compound_execution.subagent_policy: invoke_subagent is reserved strictly for divergent research, broad exploratory repository searches, or independent background sidecars.

multi_agent.description: Isolated parallel subagents via platform API (Antigravity invoke_subagent). Used selectively for divergent exploration, broad codebase research, or independent background sidecars.

sequential_persona.description: Single-agent sequential persona switching with prompt-modulated thinking budgets. Used in GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or single-model environments where subagent forking is unavailable.

tier_1_deep_reasoning.prompt_directive: Act as [ROLE]. Activate deep extended reasoning. Exhaustively evaluate architectural invariants, failure modes, and edge cases before outputting solutions.

tier_2_analytical.prompt_directive: Act as [ROLE]. Perform systematic structural and UX analysis with focused analytical reasoning.

tier_3_balanced.prompt_directive: Act as [ROLE]. Implement clean, maintainable, and strictly specified code or tests adhering directly to Clean Architecture. Rely on compiler and testrunner feedback rather than speculative over-reasoning.

tier_4_fast_deterministic.prompt_directive: Act as [ROLE]. Execute deterministically and rapidly. Output strictly the requested command, commit message, or manifest with zero conversational overhead.

copilot.auto_routing_behavior: When Copilot model selection is set to 'Auto', GitHub dynamically routes prompts based on heuristics. Skills steer this via prompt modulation (Sequential Persona Mode) to signal high-capability reasoning for Tier 1/2 and concise execution for Tier 3/4.
